    <script>
  (function () {
    var MARK = '[data-kc-surface]';
    var ROLES = { page: 1, accent: 1, transition: 1 };

    function resolve() {
      var edge = null;
      var wrappers = document.querySelectorAll('#MainContent > .shopify-section, .shopify-section-group-footer-group');
      for (var i = 0; i < wrappers.length; i++) {
        var wrapper = wrappers[i];
        var el = wrapper.querySelector('[data-kc-surface]');
        if (!el) {
          if (wrapper.querySelector(':scope > :not(script, style, link, template, noscript)')) edge = 'page';
          continue;
        }
        var role = el.getAttribute('data-kc-surface');
        if (!ROLES[role]) role = 'page';
        if (edge === null) edge = role === 'accent' ? 'accent' : 'page';
        var bottom = role === 'transition' ? (edge === 'page' ? 'accent' : 'page') : role;
        wrapper.setAttribute('data-kc-edge-top', edge);
        wrapper.setAttribute('data-kc-edge-bottom', bottom);
        if (role !== 'transition' && role !== edge) {
          wrapper.setAttribute(
            'data-kc-seam',
            'Section surface ' + role + ' follows ' + edge + ': shown as ' + edge + ' → ' + role
          );
        } else {
          wrapper.removeAttribute('data-kc-seam');
        }
        edge = bottom;
      }
    }

    function touchesSurfaces(records) {
      for (var i = 0; i < records.length; i++) {
        var lists = [records[i].addedNodes, records[i].removedNodes];
        for (var l = 0; l < lists.length; l++) {
          for (var j = 0; j < lists[l].length; j++) {
            var node = lists[l][j];
            if (node.nodeType !== 1) continue;
            if (node.matches('.shopify-section, ' + MARK) || node.querySelector(MARK)) return true;
          }
        }
      }
      return false;
    }

    new MutationObserver(function (records) {
      if (touchesSurfaces(records)) resolve();
    }).observe(document.documentElement, { childList: true, subtree: true });
    document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', resolve);
    window.KCSurface = { resolve: resolve };
  })();
</script>

    <script src="//www.karmicare.com/cdn/shop/t/35/assets/kc-cookie-preferences.js?v=75340682069008201121792060976" defer="defer"></script><style id="karmicare-button-styles">
  /* ── KC BUTTON COLOURS (Victor, 20 Oct), from assets/kc-tokens.css. Set on body, where the
     Day/Night token values live; every KC button (sections and assets) reads these.
     Primary: navy by Day, light by Night (surface/inverse). Pressed takes the next step on the
     same ramp (border/primary/default-hover: #2c3a60 Day, #dddbd9 Night). Secondary: no fill,
     the control border, KC/Button Secondary hover and pressed. ── */
  body {
    --button-kc-primary-bg: var(--kc-mapped-surface-inverse-default);
    --button-kc-primary-text: var(--kc-mapped-text-inverse-default);
    --button-kc-primary-bg-hover: var(--kc-mapped-surface-inverse-default-hover);
    --button-kc-primary-bg-pressed: var(--kc-mapped-border-primary-default-hover);
    --button-kc-secondary-border: var(--kc-mapped-border-control-default);
    --button-kc-secondary-bg-hover: var(--kc-mapped-surface-primary-default-hover);
    --button-kc-secondary-bg-pressed: var(--kc-mapped-surface-tertiary-default);
  }

  .karmicare__btn-primary,
  .karmicare__btn-secondary {
    display: inline-flex;
    align-items: center;
    justify-content: center;
    padding: 1.35rem 1.5rem;
    border-radius: var(--primary-border-radius);
    font-weight: var(--font-700-weight);
    text-transform: uppercase;
    letter-spacing: var(--kc-responsive-Nunito-letter-spacing);
    font-size: var(--font-body-small-size-desktop);
    cursor: pointer;
    transition: background-color .2s ease, color .2s ease, border-color .2s ease;
    box-sizing: border-box;
    line-height: normal;
    text-decoration: none;
    border: 1px solid transparent;
    text-align: center;
    font-family: var(--kc-font-family-Nunito);
  }

  .karmicare__btn-secondary,
  body.night-mode .karmicare__btn-secondary {
    background: transparent;
    border: 1px solid var(--button-kc-secondary-border);
  }

  .karmicare__btn-primary {
    background-color: var(--button-kc-primary-bg);
    color: var(--button-kc-primary-text);
  }

  /* ── HEADER BEGIN NOW (DAY MODE): keeps the theme-setting colours ── */
  body.day-mode .header__cta-btn.karmicare__btn-primary,
  body:not(.night-mode) .header__cta-btn.karmicare__btn-primary {background-color: #7FB9FF;color: #0A1628;}

  /* ── SECONDARY BUTTON (DAY MODE) ── */
  body.day-mode .karmicare__btn-secondary,
  body:not(.night-mode) .karmicare__btn-secondary {color: #191F38;}

  /* ── HEADER BEGIN NOW (NIGHT MODE) ── */
  body.night-mode .header__cta-btn.karmicare__btn-primary {background-color: #7FB9FF;color: #191F38;}

  /* ── SECONDARY BUTTON (NIGHT MODE) ── */
  body.night-mode .karmicare__btn-secondary {color: #FFFBF6;}

  /* ── INTERACTION STATES: colour only, no motion, on every primary and secondary button,
     "Coming soon" ones included. Header BEGIN NOW: sections/header.liquid. ── */
  body .karmicare__btn-primary:hover {
    background-color: var(--button-kc-primary-bg-hover);
  }
  body .karmicare__btn-primary:active {
    background-color: var(--button-kc-primary-bg-pressed);
  }
  body .karmicare__btn-secondary:hover {
    background-color: var(--button-kc-secondary-bg-hover);
  }
  body .karmicare__btn-secondary:active {
    background-color: var(--button-kc-secondary-bg-pressed);
  }
  .karmicare__btn-primary:focus-visible,
  .karmicare__btn-secondary:focus-visible {
    outline: 2px solid var(--kc-mapped-border-focus-strong);
    outline-offset: 2px;
  }

  .karmicare__btn-primary svg,.karmicare__btn-secondary svg{margin-left:10px;}
  /* KC/Button (medium): 20px side padding on desktop */
  @media screen and (min-width: 990px) {
    .karmicare__btn-primary,
    .karmicare__btn-secondary {
      padding-left: 2rem;
      padding-right: 2rem;
    }
  }
  @media screen and (max-width: 749px) {
    .karmicare__btn-primary,
    .karmicare__btn-secondary {
      font-size: var(--font-body-small-size-mobile);
      padding: 1.2rem 1.2rem;
    }
  }

  /* ── DAWN BUTTONS (.button) follow the KC buttons (Victor, 20 Oct): cart, account, search,
     password, contact and other standard pages. Tertiary (icon and remove buttons) keeps
     Dawn's look. Dawn draws its border and hover with ::before/::after shadows; those go. ── */
  .button:not(.button--tertiary),
  .shopify-challenge__button {
    border-radius: var(--kc-shape-radius-sm);
    background-color: var(--button-kc-primary-bg);
    color: var(--button-kc-primary-text);
    box-shadow: none;
    font-family: var(--kc-font-role-identity);
    font-weight: 700;
    font-size: var(--kc-responsive-label-lg-text-size);
    letter-spacing: var(--kc-responsive-Nunito-letter-spacing);
    text-transform: uppercase;
    transition: background-color .2s ease, color .2s ease;
  }
  .button:not(.button--tertiary)::before,
  .button:not(.button--tertiary)::after,
  .shopify-challenge__button::before,
  .shopify-challenge__button::after {
    box-shadow: none !important;
  }
  .button.button--secondary {
    background-color: transparent;
    color: var(--kc-mapped-text-default-heading);
    border: 1px solid var(--button-kc-secondary-border);
  }
  .button:not(.button--tertiary):not(.button--secondary):not([disabled]):hover,
  .shopify-challenge__button:hover {
    background-color: var(--button-kc-primary-bg-hover);
  }
  .button:not(.button--tertiary):not(.button--secondary):not([disabled]):active,
  .shopify-challenge__button:active {
    background-color: var(--button-kc-primary-bg-pressed);
  }
  .button.button--secondary:not([disabled]):hover {
    background-color: var(--button-kc-secondary-bg-hover);
  }
  .button.button--secondary:not([disabled]):active {
    background-color: var(--button-kc-secondary-bg-pressed);
  }
  .button:not(.button--tertiary):focus-visible {
    outline: 2px solid var(--kc-mapped-border-focus-strong);
    outline-offset: 2px;
    box-shadow: none;
  }

  /* ── LOADING (R13 F1): the label hides again and the spinner takes the button's text colour.
     The colour rule above, and the buybox and end CTA ones (kc-buybox.css,
     section-featured-product.css), outrank Dawn's .button.loading; Dawn's spinner reads the
     saved scheme's --color-button-text. body lifts these above all of them. A pending button is
     also disabled (karmi-add-to-cart.js); it stays opaque so the spinner keeps its contrast,
     and the disabled attribute still blocks clicks. The label wrappers hide by opacity, which
     forced colours leave alone and which keeps the accessible name. ── */
  body .button.loading:not(.button--tertiary) {
    color: transparent;
    opacity: 1;
  }
  body .button.loading:not(.button--tertiary) > :not(.loading__spinner) {
    opacity: 0;
  }
  body .button.loading:not(.button--tertiary):not(.button--secondary) > .loading__spinner .path {
    stroke: var(--button-kc-primary-text);
  }
  body .button.button--secondary.loading > .loading__spinner .path {
    stroke: var(--kc-mapped-text-default-heading);
  }
  @media screen and (forced-colors: active) {
    body .button.loading:not(.button--tertiary):not(.button--secondary) > .loading__spinner .path,
    body .button.button--secondary.loading > .loading__spinner .path {
      stroke: ButtonText;
    }
  }
</style>

<p><strong>Self reflection:</strong></p>
<ul>
<li aria-level="1">Does the toothpaste I’m using support my oral health?</li>
<li aria-level="1">How can I use brushing my teeth in the morning and evening as a way to nourish my body?</li>
<li aria-level="1">Is there a way to safely remineralize my teeth and enhance my smile?</li>
</ul>
<p><strong>Key takeaways:</strong></p>
<ul>
<li aria-level="1">
<span>Nano hydroxyapatite</span><span> has powerful </span><span>remineralizing effects</span><span> on enamel </span><span>lesions</span><span> while being safe, </span><span>nontoxic</span><span>, and </span><span>fluoride-free</span><span>.</span>
</li>
<li aria-level="1">
<span>A </span><span>review of literature</span><span> found </span><span>nano hydroxyapatite</span><span> is an effective </span><span>remineralizing agent</span><span>, and demonstrates impressive </span><span>desensitizing</span><span> properties.</span>
</li>
<li aria-level="1">
<span>Choosing a natural toothpaste </span><span>formulation</span><span> with </span><span>nano hydroxyapatite</span><span> can help prevent </span><span>tooth decay</span><span>, </span><span>whiten</span><span> teeth without increasing </span><span>tooth sensitivity</span><span>, and improve overall oral hygiene.</span>
</li>
</ul>
<blockquote>
<p><strong>“There’s no fluoride in our Awake or Asleep toothpaste. Nor will there ever be.”<br></strong><i><span>— Victor Popov, Founder of Karmicare</span></i></p>
<p><i><span><meta charset="utf-8"> <b>WHY?</b> Because as well as resisting negative self-talk, I avoid putting chemicals into my system. Especially chemicals that prevent natural healing and spiritual growth. And especially when there are far more powerful ingredients available.Ingredients such as hydroxyapatite. I know, I can hear you thinking hydroxy-what? You may not have heard of it but it makes up 97% of your tooth enamel. Its “nano” form (as first discovered by NASA) can fuse with your enamel, replace lost minerals, whiten teeth, reduce sensitivity and much, much more. In short, it could be the answer to your dental health problems. Want your teeth to constantly feel stronger, healthier, smoother, and resistant to the sudden jolt/pain of hot and cold drinks? Swap fluoride for nano HAp. I’ve experienced these benefits myself, which is why I call it the “wonder-mineral” and that’s why it’s one of the stars of Karmicare’s biorhythmic formulated toothpaste.</span></i></p>
</blockquote>
<p><meta charset="UTF-8">Read on and discover everything you need to know about this medical marvel for better teeth, bones and overall health. It’s research-based and the claims are factual.</p>
<h1><span>10-Second Nano HAp Need-to-Know Truths</span></h1>
<ul>
<li aria-level="1"><span>Nano HAp dives into your enamel and refills the lost minerals every time you brush your teeth</span></li>
<li aria-level="1">
<span>It smoothes and </span><span>whitens</span><span> teeth by gently repairing your </span><span>tooth surface</span><span> with native minerals</span>
</li>
<li aria-level="1">
<span>It plugs exposed </span><span>dentin tubules</span><span> to effectively reduce </span><span>tooth sensitivity</span><br>
</li>
<li aria-level="1"><span>It helps protect against tooth decay and harmful dietary acids</span></li>
<li aria-level="1">
<span>It’s </span><span>bioactive</span><span>, osteoconductive, and </span><span>nontoxic</span>
</li>
<li aria-level="1"><span>And much more — skip to our frequently asked questions to learn more little-known facts</span></li>
</ul>
<h2><span>Expand Your Dental Knowledge</span></h2>
<p><b>Enamel<span> </span></b><span>— </span><i><span>the outer shell of the tooth that protects against </span></i><i><span>tooth decay</span></i><i><span>. Ninety-seven percent of the enamel is made of hydroxyapatite (HA).</span></i></p>
<p><b>Dentin</b><span> — </span><i><span>the second layer of the tooth situated right under the enamel. Seventy percent of dentin is made of HA.</span></i></p>
<p><b>Dentin tubules</b><b><span> </span></b><span>— </span><i><span>microscopic channels that connect the </span></i><i><span>enamel surface</span></i><i><span> to the dental pulp. These channels travel through </span></i><i><span>dentin</span></i><i><span> all the way to the tooth nerve, hence the name </span></i><i><span>dentin tubules.</span></i></p>
<p><b>Tooth erosion<span> </span></b><span>— </span><i><span>refers to the loss of </span></i><i><span>tooth enamel</span></i><i><span> due to exposure to acid.</span></i></p>
<p><b>Micropores<span> </span></b><span>— </span><i><span>the enamel might look smooth but has thousands of pores. It’s these pores that absorb stains from the food and drinks you consume.</span></i></p>
<p><b>Enamel<span> </span></b><b>lesions</b><b><span> </span></b><span>— </span><i><span>any damage or abnormal change to enamel.</span></i></p>
<p><b>Dental pulp<span> </span></b><span>—</span><i><span> the innermost part of the tooth. It’s soft and full of nerves and blood vessels.</span></i></p>
<p><b>Hydroxyapatite<span> </span></b><span>— </span><i><span>a naturally occurring mineral form of </span></i><i><span>calcium</span></i><i><span> </span></i><i><span>apatite</span></i><i><span> (</span></i><i><span>calcium</span></i><i><span>, phosphorous oxygen) that makes up most of our bones.</span></i></p>
<p><b>Nano hydroxyapatite</b><b><span> </span></b><span>— </span><i><span>nano-sized version of hydroxyapatite that’s commonly used in </span></i><i><span>dentistry</span></i><i><span>, osteopathy, and orthopedics because of its </span></i><i><span>remineralizing</span></i><i><span> and repairing properties.</span></i></p>
<p><b>Micro HAp<span> </span></b><span>— </span><i><span>particles of HA that are slightly bigger than nano HAp.</span></i></p>
<h1>So, What Is Nano Hydroxyapatite?</h1>
<p><i><span><img alt="Charcoal toothbrush" src="https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0765/7586/7189/files/charcoal-toothbrushes_600x600.jpg?v=1697123947"></span></i></p>
<p><br></p>
<p><span>“Hydroxy-WHAT?!” — we get it.</span><br><span>It’s a bit of a mouthful to speak and to spell.</span><br><span>But while it may seem strange to you, your body is highly familiar with this magic mineral.</span><br><span>Hydroxyapatite (HA) is a naturally occurring form of </span><span>calcium phosphate </span><span>(so no need for the synthesis of ingredients in a lab) that makes up 97% of your </span><span>tooth enamel</span><span>, 70% of </span><span>dentin</span><span>, and up to 70% of bone mass. It’s also found in your saliva. And because it’s a natural substance, hydroxyapatite is often used in biomimetic dentistry, which aims to protect the integrity of your teeth. The primary purpose of HA is to give bones and teeth their rigidity.</span><br><a href="https://karmicare.com/en/why-use-hydroxyapatite-toothpaste"><span>Nano hydroxyapatite</span></a><span> (nano HAp) is an altered version of HA that has the natural ability to fuse with the existing hydroxyapatite in teeth.</span></p>
<p><br></p>
<p><span>There are a few essential characteristics of nano HAp that make this mineral so indispensable to our </span><span>oral health</span><span>. Nano HAp is:</span></p>
<ul>
<li aria-level="1">
<b>Biocompatible</b><b><span> </span></b><span>— It exists in harmony with its surrounding tissues.</span>
</li>
<li aria-level="1">
<b>Bioactive</b><b><span> </span></b><span>— Nano HAp is already in a bioavailable, usable form.</span>
</li>
<li aria-level="1">
<b>Osteoconductive<span> </span></b><span>— Nano HAp serves as a scaffold for new bone growth.</span>
</li>
<li aria-level="1">
<b>Nontoxic</b><b><span> </span>and non-inflammatory<span> </span></b><span>— Since hydroxyapatite is a naturally occurring organic biomaterial in our body, nano HAp does not cause toxicity or inflammation.</span>
</li>
</ul>
<h3><span>Formed By Nature. Refined By NASA. Utilized By Karmicare.</span></h3>
<p><span>Nano hydroxyapatite</span><span> has a colorful history that spans across four decades. Believe it or not, </span><span>NASA</span><span> was the inventor of the first version of </span><span>nano hydroxyapatite</span><span> in 1970.</span></p>
<p><span>Why would a space agency spend their time creating nano HAp?</span></p>
<p><span>The astronauts returning home from the space mission were experiencing mineral loss from teeth and bones as a result of staying in a zero-gravity environment. Nano HAp was created as a repairing material to restore what was lost. With the help of nanotechnology, scientists have discovered a way to turn hydroxyapatite into nanoparticles that go to work remineralizing your teeth.</span></p>
<p><span>Since then, nano HAp has cemented itself as the hallmark in the medical field and in </span><span>oral care</span><span> globally, especially in </span><span>Japan</span><span> and Europe.</span></p>
<p><span>But sadly, it’s not widely available in the mainstream. This is something we want to see changed, especially when the big brands are spending billions on marketing but still using toxins in their toothpaste.</span></p>
<h1><span>4 Powerful Benefits of Nano Hydroxyapatite</span></h1>
<p><span><img alt="Woman with orange" src="https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0765/7586/7189/files/woman-holds-orange_600x600.jpg?v=1697124034"></span></p>
<h2><span>1. Renews Your Teeth From the Inside Out</span></h2>
<p><span>Your teeth have microscopic holes (known as </span><span>dentin tubules</span><span>) present throughout the underside of the enamel. Minerals and other substances, like good and bad microbes, use these tubules to travel in and out of your teeth.</span></p>
<p><span>When you indulge in sweet food or drink, the sugar-loving microbes metabolize the sugar and release acids as waste products. Accumulation of these acids triggers the pH level in your mouth to drop to or below 5.5.</span></p>
<p><span><meta charset="UTF-8"> <b>FYI:</b> The pH level in <a href="https://karmicare.com/en/product/biorhythmic-oral-hygiene-set">Karmicare Biorhythmic Oral Health</a> (both the Awake and Asleep formulations) is between 6.5-7.5.</span></p>
<p><span>Such an acidic environment is caustic to both enamel and </span><span>dentin</span><span> because it dissolves </span><span>calcium</span><span> and phosphate </span><span>ions</span><span>. </span></p>
<p><span>This is known as </span><span>demineralization</span><span>.</span></p>
<p><span>Since enamel isn’t a living tissue, it cannot regrow. But slight damage can be repaired through </span><span>remineralization</span><span>.</span></p>
<p><span>It turns out that our body has its own natural buffer system — saliva. It prevents the pH level from getting too low by neutralizing the acids. Also, saliva contains many critical components that our teeth need, including </span><span>calcium</span><span>, phosphorus, </span><span>protein</span><span>, enzymes, and bicarbonates.</span></p>
<p><span>Saliva keeps our enamel continuously bathed in a nourishing solution.</span></p>
<p><span>But relying on saliva isn’t enough. You must take proactive measures to </span><a href="https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC4252862/"><span>promote </span><span>remineralization</span></a><span> by using a </span><span>nano hydroxyapatite toothpaste</span><span>. Along with </span><span>nano hydroxyapatite</span><span>, look for a natural toothpaste with other oral hygiene-friendly ingredients such as</span><a href="https://www.cda.org/portals/0/pdfs/fact_sheets/xylitol_english.pdf"><span> </span><span>xylitol</span></a><span>. This natural sugar alcohol inhibits the growth of bacteria that can cause carious </span><span>lesions. Better known as a cavity</span><span>, a carious lesion is the visible breakdown of the tooth’s surface structures</span><span>.</span></p>
<p><span>Keep in mind there are other reasons to be choosy with your toothpaste selection. Preservatives and other additives (like sodium laureth sulfate) may not only harm your oral microbiome, but also be hard on your body. Using </span><span>fluoride-free</span><span>toothpaste and stepping up your oral hygiene is an easy way to start mindfully nourishing your body inside and out.</span></p>
<p><strong>How Nano HAp Repairs Your Teeth</strong></p>
<p><span>Whenever you brush your teeth with a nano HAp toothpaste, it replaces the lost minerals by binding with the existing hydroxyapatite, thereby increasing the eroded tooth’s microhardness.</span></p>
<p><span>An in </span><span>vitro study</span><span> using a </span><span>scanning electron</span><span> microscope (</span><span>SEM</span><span>) found a “formation of </span><a href="https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S2090123213000325"><span>bone-like apatite layer on composite surfaces</span></a>.<span>" </span><span>Dentifrice</span><span> </span><span>formulations (like toothpaste and remineralizing tooth powders)</span><span> that include </span><span>nano hydroxyapatite</span><span>instead of </span><span>fluoride</span><span> may be more supportive of </span><span>enamel remineralization</span><span>.</span></p>
<p><span>Nano HAp penetrates the enamel’s surface area and directly restores the amount of </span><span>calcium</span><span> and phosphates in areas where it has been dissolved.</span></p>
<p><span>It also fills up the microscopic fissures present on the </span><span>enamel surface</span><span>. Nano HAp’s innate </span><span>biocompatibility</span><span> ensures there are no harmful side effects like </span><span>fluoride</span><span>.</span></p>
<h2><span>2. Nano Hydroxyapatite Whitens Your Teeth Without Hurting Your Enamel</span></h2>
<p><span>Stained yellow teeth are like a scarlet chain of shame for many people.</span></p>
<p><span>They are reminded of it every time they look in the mirror, pose for a photo, or go for an interview. And can’t offer a confident smile with their handshake, or openly laugh at a friend’s jokes.</span></p>
<p><span>From buying an expensive teeth </span><span>whitening</span><span> kit to brushing with baking soda to using apple cider vinegar or even rubbing the teeth with strawberries, there aren’t many things people won’t do to get their bright smile back.</span></p>
<p><span>Most of the products available only give temporary results and leave behind a weak and </span><span>demineralized</span><span> enamel.</span></p>
<p><span>Bleaching agents like hydrogen peroxide cause </span><span>tooth sensitivity</span><span> and chemical burns. So while you’ll have whiter teeth, your sensitive teeth may leave you wincing in pain when eating or drinking. Hydrogen peroxide also alters the enamel structure by breaking down </span><span>proteins</span><span>.</span></p>
<p><span>Other </span><span>whitening</span><span> toothpaste has minute particles that work like sandpaper, exfoliating the stains from teeth. By using such products for a long time, you are physically scraping away superficial layers of your enamel.</span></p>
<p><span>Low-abrasive toothpastes (like Karmicare) that contain nano HAp are a far safer alternative to commercially available </span><span>whitening</span><span> products. It doesn’t harm the structural integrity of the enamel through exfoliation. On the contrary, nano HAp </span><span>remineralizes</span><span> the tooth from the inside out. And gentle ingredients like calcium carbonate and perlite help gently polish your teeth to a sparkling white. A </span><a href="https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/15509084/"><span>study of 600 subjects with tooth stains</span></a><span> found toothpaste with calcium carbonate removed more stains than standard toothpaste over four weeks of twice-daily brushing.</span></p>
<p><strong>How Nano HAp Whitens Your Teeth</strong></p>
<p><span>Nano HAp </span><span>remineralizes</span><span> teeth from the inside, which smooths the tooth’s surface and makes it glossier.</span></p>
<p><span>The </span><span>whitening</span><span> effect of nano HAp on teeth is not the result of a mechanical or chemical reaction.</span></p>

                document.querySelectorAll('.unified-loc-link').forEach(function (link) {

                    e.preventDefault();
                    var type = this.getAttribute('data-type');
                    var val = this.getAttribute('data-value');
                    var form = document.getElementById('FooterUnifiedLocalizationForm');

                    if (type === 'language') {
                      document.getElementById('UnifiedLocaleCode').value = val;
                    } else if (type === 'country') {
                      document.getElementById('UnifiedCountryCode').value = val;
                    }

                    form.submit();
                  });
                });

                // Close dropdown when clicking outside
                document.addEventListener('click', function (e) {
                  var form = document.getElementById('FooterUnifiedLocalizationForm');
                  if (form && !form.contains(e.target)) {
                    var wrapper = form.querySelector('.disclosure__list-wrapper');
                    var btn = form.querySelector('.disclosure__button');
                    if (wrapper && !wrapper.hasAttribute('hidden')) {
                      wrapper.setAttribute('hidden', '');
                      btn.setAttribute('aria-expanded', 'false');
                    }
                  }
                });

  <script>
    (function () {
      const BUNDLE_PRODUCT_IDS = [
        

            15977093923197,
          
        

            16002518417789,
          
        

            16004862902653
          
        
      ];

      const FREE_PRODUCTS = [
        

            {
              productId: 16052623442301
            },
          
        

            {
              productId: 16052623278461
            },
          
        

            {
              productId: 7784767357110
            }
          
        
      ];

      const DISCOUNT_CODE = 'Welcome Kit';

      if (FREE_PRODUCTS.length === 0 || BUNDLE_PRODUCT_IDS.length === 0) return;

      const customerAlreadyReceivedFreeProduct = false;
      let isUpdating = false;

      async function getCart() {
        const res = await fetch('/cart.js');
        return res.json();
      }

      // A subscription without exactly its kit nested under it (missing, loose, out of order, under another
      // line or more than one of a kit line: a cart from outside the theme or from before the kit was nested;
      // every add path of the theme brings the kit in its own add). On a page that sells the plan product,
      // assets/kc-plan-select.js repairKit puts the whole kit under the plan line in cart order and leaves
      // the plan line as it is; it reads the full cart and changes nothing when the kit is in place.
      // Elsewhere the cart stays as it is.
      async function repairKit() {
        if (!window.KCPlanSelect) return false;
        try {
          if (!(await window.KCPlanSelect.repairKit())) return false;
          await applyDiscountCode();
          return true;
        } catch (e) {
          return false;
        }
      }

      async function applyDiscountCode() {
        try {
          await fetch('/cart/update.js', {
            method: 'POST',
            headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json', 'X-Karmi-Sync': 'false' },
            body: JSON.stringify({ discount: DISCOUNT_CODE }),
          });
        } catch (e) {}
      }

      async function syncFreeProduct(providedCart) {
        if (isUpdating) return;
        isUpdating = true;

        try {
          const cart = (providedCart && Array.isArray(providedCart.items)) ? providedCart : await getCart();
          const items = cart.items || [];

          const hasBundleSubscription = items.some((item) =>
            BUNDLE_PRODUCT_IDS.includes(item.product_id) &&
            Boolean(
              item.selling_plan_allocation ||
              (item.selling_plan_id && !isNaN(parseInt(item.selling_plan_id)) && parseInt(item.selling_plan_id) > 0)
            )
          );

          let cartChanged = false;

          if (customerAlreadyReceivedFreeProduct || !hasBundleSubscription) {
            const updates = {};
            for (const freeProd of FREE_PRODUCTS) {
              const freeLineItem = items.find((item) =>
                item.product_id === freeProd.productId &&
                item.properties &&
                item.properties['_welcome_kit'] === 'true'
              );
              if (freeLineItem) {
                updates[freeLineItem.key] = 0;
              }
            }
            // "Subscription Name" (Care Credit) belongs to a subscription in the cart: clear it once none
            // is left, also when there are no kit lines to remove, and keep it while one remains
            // (only from a full cart: an add response lists just the added lines)
            const isFullCart = Boolean(cart.attributes);
            const hasAnySubscription = items.some((item) => item.selling_plan_allocation);
            const staleSubscriptionName = isFullCart && !hasAnySubscription && cart.attributes['Subscription Name'];
            if (Object.keys(updates).length > 0 || staleSubscriptionName) {
              const body = Object.keys(updates).length > 0 ? { updates: updates, discount: '' } : {};
              if (isFullCart && !hasAnySubscription) body.attributes = { 'Subscription Name': '' };
              await fetch('/cart/update.js', {
                method: 'POST',
                headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json', 'X-Karmi-Sync': 'false' },
                body: JSON.stringify(body),
              });
              cartChanged = true;
            }
          } else {
            // repairKit checks the full cart: the plan line, each kit line once, its quantity, order, parent
            cartChanged = await repairKit();
          }

          if (cartChanged) {
            refreshCartDrawer();
          }
        } finally {
          isUpdating = false;
        }
      }

      function refreshCartDrawer() {
        document.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent('cart:refresh'));
        if (typeof window.refreshDawnCartUI === 'function') {
          window.refreshDawnCartUI().catch(() => {});
        } else if (typeof window.Shopify !== 'undefined') {
          fetch('/cart.js')
            .then((r) => r.json())
            .then((cart) => {
              document.dispatchEvent(
                new CustomEvent('cart:updated', { detail: { cart } })
              );
            });
        }
      }

      const originalFetch = window.fetch;
      window.fetch = async function (...args) {
        const options = args[1] || {};
        const headers = options.headers || {};
        const isInternalSync = headers['X-Karmi-Sync'] === 'false';

        const response = await originalFetch.apply(this, args);
        const url = typeof args[0] === 'string' ? args[0] : args[0]?.url || '';
        if (
          !isInternalSync &&
          (url.includes('/cart/add') ||
          url.includes('/cart/change') ||
          url.includes('/cart/update'))
        ) {
          response.clone().json().then((cartData) => {
            syncFreeProduct(cartData && Array.isArray(cartData.items) ? cartData : null);
          }).catch(() => {
            syncFreeProduct();
          });
        }
        return response;
      };

      document.addEventListener('cart:updated', syncFreeProduct);
      document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', syncFreeProduct);
      window.karmiWelcomeKitSync = syncFreeProduct;

      window.addEventListener('pageshow', (event) => {
        const isBackNavigation = event.persisted ||
          (window.performance && window.performance.navigation && window.performance.navigation.type === 2);
        if (isBackNavigation) {
          refreshCartDrawer();
        }
      });
    })();
  </script>

    <script>
  (function () {
    var MARK = '[data-kc-surface]';
    var ROLES = { page: 1, accent: 1, transition: 1 };

    function resolve() {
      var edge = null;
      var wrappers = document.querySelectorAll('#MainContent > .shopify-section, .shopify-section-group-footer-group');
      for (var i = 0; i < wrappers.length; i++) {
        var wrapper = wrappers[i];
        var el = wrapper.querySelector('[data-kc-surface]');
        if (!el) {
          if (wrapper.querySelector(':scope > :not(script, style, link, template, noscript)')) edge = 'page';
          continue;
        }
        var role = el.getAttribute('data-kc-surface');
        if (!ROLES[role]) role = 'page';
        if (edge === null) edge = role === 'accent' ? 'accent' : 'page';
        var bottom = role === 'transition' ? (edge === 'page' ? 'accent' : 'page') : role;
        wrapper.setAttribute('data-kc-edge-top', edge);
        wrapper.setAttribute('data-kc-edge-bottom', bottom);
        if (role !== 'transition' && role !== edge) {
          wrapper.setAttribute(
            'data-kc-seam',
            'Section surface ' + role + ' follows ' + edge + ': shown as ' + edge + ' → ' + role
          );
        } else {
          wrapper.removeAttribute('data-kc-seam');
        }
        edge = bottom;
      }
    }

    function touchesSurfaces(records) {
      for (var i = 0; i < records.length; i++) {
        var lists = [records[i].addedNodes, records[i].removedNodes];
        for (var l = 0; l < lists.length; l++) {
          for (var j = 0; j < lists[l].length; j++) {
            var node = lists[l][j];
            if (node.nodeType !== 1) continue;
            if (node.matches('.shopify-section, ' + MARK) || node.querySelector(MARK)) return true;
          }
        }
      }
      return false;
    }

    new MutationObserver(function (records) {
      if (touchesSurfaces(records)) resolve();
    }).observe(document.documentElement, { childList: true, subtree: true });
    document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', resolve);
    window.KCSurface = { resolve: resolve };
  })();
</script>

  .km-footer-legal__links a {

    text-decoration: underline;
    text-underline-offset: 0.15em;
  }

  .km-footer-legal__links a:hover {

  .km-footer-payments {
    display: flex;
    flex-wrap: wrap;

  /* The payment methods switched on in Shopify, in the Figma footer's monochrome style
     (Victor, 21 Oct, G-5). Grayscale only: each identifying mark keeps at least 3:1 on its
     own opaque chip, Day and Night alike (lowest: Mastercard's right circle 3.36:1 with the
     rule below, then Maestro 3.74:1); softening it further drops MobilePay below 3:1
     (R15 F2). */
  .km-footer-payments svg {
    display: block;
    width: 38px;
    height: 24px;
    filter: grayscale(1);
  }

  /* Mastercard's red circle turns 1.30:1 on its dark chip in grayscale (R15b F2): a light chip
     like the others, with both circles and their overlap in greys that stay apart and each
     clear 3:1 on white (#595959 7.0:1, #8c8c8c 3.4:1, #333 12.6:1). Its colours are inline
     styles (display-p3 included), hence !important. Paths: outer chip, inner chip, left
     circle, right circle, overlap. */
  .km-footer-payments svg[aria-labelledby='pi-master'] path:nth-of-type(1) {
    fill: #ededed !important;
  }
  .km-footer-payments svg[aria-labelledby='pi-master'] path:nth-of-type(2) {
    fill: #ffffff !important;
  }
  .km-footer-payments svg[aria-labelledby='pi-master'] path:nth-of-type(3) {
    fill: #595959 !important;
  }
  .km-footer-payments svg[aria-labelledby='pi-master'] path:nth-of-type(4) {
    fill: #8c8c8c !important;
  }
  .km-footer-payments svg[aria-labelledby='pi-master'] path:nth-of-type(5) {
    fill: #333333 !important;
  }

  <script>
    (function () {
      const BUNDLE_PRODUCT_IDS = [

            16002518417789,
          
        

            16004862902653
          
        
      ];

      const FREE_PRODUCTS = [
        

            {
              productId: 16052623442301
            },
          
        

            {
              productId: 16052623278461
            },
          
        

            {
              productId: 7784767357110
            }
          
        
      ];

      const DISCOUNT_CODE = 'Welcome Kit';

      if (FREE_PRODUCTS.length === 0 || BUNDLE_PRODUCT_IDS.length === 0) return;

      const customerAlreadyReceivedFreeProduct = false;
      let isUpdating = false;

      async function getCart() {
        const res = await fetch('/cart.js');
        return res.json();
      }

      // A subscription without exactly its kit nested under it (missing, loose, out of order, under another
      // line or more than one of a kit line: a cart from outside the theme or from before the kit was nested;
      // every add path of the theme brings the kit in its own add). On a page that sells the plan product,
      // assets/kc-plan-select.js repairKit puts the whole kit under the plan line in cart order and leaves
      // the plan line as it is; it reads the full cart and changes nothing when the kit is in place.
      // Elsewhere the cart stays as it is.
      async function repairKit() {
        if (!window.KCPlanSelect) return false;
        try {
          if (!(await window.KCPlanSelect.repairKit())) return false;
          await applyDiscountCode();
          return true;
        } catch (e) {
          return false;
        }
      }

      async function applyDiscountCode() {
        try {
          await fetch('/cart/update.js', {
            method: 'POST',
            headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json', 'X-Karmi-Sync': 'false' },
            body: JSON.stringify({ discount: DISCOUNT_CODE }),
          });
        } catch (e) {}
      }

      async function syncFreeProduct(providedCart) {
        if (isUpdating) return;
        isUpdating = true;

        try {
          const cart = (providedCart && Array.isArray(providedCart.items)) ? providedCart : await getCart();
          const items = cart.items || [];

          const hasBundleSubscription = items.some((item) =>
            BUNDLE_PRODUCT_IDS.includes(item.product_id) &&
            Boolean(
              item.selling_plan_allocation ||
              (item.selling_plan_id && !isNaN(parseInt(item.selling_plan_id)) && parseInt(item.selling_plan_id) > 0)
            )
          );

          let cartChanged = false;

          if (customerAlreadyReceivedFreeProduct || !hasBundleSubscription) {
            const updates = {};
            for (const freeProd of FREE_PRODUCTS) {
              const freeLineItem = items.find((item) =>
                item.product_id === freeProd.productId &&
                item.properties &&
                item.properties['_welcome_kit'] === 'true'
              );
              if (freeLineItem) {
                updates[freeLineItem.key] = 0;
              }
            }
            // "Subscription Name" (Care Credit) belongs to a subscription in the cart: clear it once none
            // is left, also when there are no kit lines to remove, and keep it while one remains
            // (only from a full cart: an add response lists just the added lines)
            const isFullCart = Boolean(cart.attributes);
            const hasAnySubscription = items.some((item) => item.selling_plan_allocation);
            const staleSubscriptionName = isFullCart && !hasAnySubscription && cart.attributes['Subscription Name'];
            if (Object.keys(updates).length > 0 || staleSubscriptionName) {
              const body = Object.keys(updates).length > 0 ? { updates: updates, discount: '' } : {};
              if (isFullCart && !hasAnySubscription) body.attributes = { 'Subscription Name': '' };
              await fetch('/cart/update.js', {
                method: 'POST',
                headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json', 'X-Karmi-Sync': 'false' },
                body: JSON.stringify(body),
              });
              cartChanged = true;
            }
          } else {
            // repairKit checks the full cart: the plan line, each kit line once, its quantity, order, parent
            cartChanged = await repairKit();
          }

          if (cartChanged) {
            refreshCartDrawer();
          }
        } finally {
          isUpdating = false;
        }
      }

      function refreshCartDrawer() {
        document.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent('cart:refresh'));
        if (typeof window.refreshDawnCartUI === 'function') {
          window.refreshDawnCartUI().catch(() => {});
        } else if (typeof window.Shopify !== 'undefined') {
          fetch('/cart.js')
            .then((r) => r.json())
            .then((cart) => {
              document.dispatchEvent(
                new CustomEvent('cart:updated', { detail: { cart } })
              );
            });
        }
      }

      const originalFetch = window.fetch;
      window.fetch = async function (...args) {
        const options = args[1] || {};
        const headers = options.headers || {};
        const isInternalSync = headers['X-Karmi-Sync'] === 'false';

        const response = await originalFetch.apply(this, args);
        const url = typeof args[0] === 'string' ? args[0] : args[0]?.url || '';
        if (
          !isInternalSync &&
          (url.includes('/cart/add') ||
          url.includes('/cart/change') ||
          url.includes('/cart/update'))
        ) {
          response.clone().json().then((cartData) => {
            syncFreeProduct(cartData && Array.isArray(cartData.items) ? cartData : null);
          }).catch(() => {
            syncFreeProduct();
          });
        }
        return response;
      };

      document.addEventListener('cart:updated', syncFreeProduct);
      document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', syncFreeProduct);
      window.karmiWelcomeKitSync = syncFreeProduct;

      window.addEventListener('pageshow', (event) => {
        const isBackNavigation = event.persisted ||
          (window.performance && window.performance.navigation && window.performance.navigation.type === 2);
        if (isBackNavigation) {
          refreshCartDrawer();
        }
      });
    })();
  </script>

benefits-of-nootropics-ease-stress-boost.title: Benefits of Nootropics: Ease Stress, Boost Focus and Improve Mood.
benefits-of-nootropics-ease-stress-boost.content:
Self-reflection:

  • Can the toothpaste I use benefit both my oral and brain health?
  • Is there a toothpaste that could help me improve my mental performance?
  • Can brushing my teeth help me stay more active during the day or get better sleep at night?

Key takeaways:

  • Nootropics are substances that optimize brain functioning, making you smarter, focused, motivated, and productive.
  • Nootropics are growing in popularity as people strive to improve their mental performance.
  • Consuming nootropics may help support better focus, memory, improved sleep quality, and reduced stress 

We live in a busy and competitive world today in which peak mental performance is crucial. Being able to learn faster, craft more effective sales pitches, score higher in games, and boost productivity in general has become a longing desire for us all. 

It's no surprise therefore that so many people are looking for ways to enhance their mental capabilities.

If this is you, you might want to consider nootropics. Nootropics promise to make you smarter, sharper, and happier. But do they work and are they worth the hype?

This article will explore the benefits of nootropics, provide examples, and highlight where you can find these powerful compounds in everyday products.

What Are Nootropics?

Nootropics are substances that may help improve cognitive functions including memory, focus, and motivation. They are also sometimes referred to as cognitive enhancers or brain boosters. 

Originally used to treat mental conditions like Alzheimer’s disease, stroke, narcolepsy, schizophrenia, ADHD, and age-related cognitive decline, these substances have shown great success. Today, many people turn to them to enhance their brain function.

There is a growing interest in nootropics, especially as people seek natural ways to improve their productivity and mental performance. While some nootropics are available as dietary supplements, others can be found in food or natural sources.

5 Benefits of Nootropics

Taking nootropics could have some positive effects on your health. Here are five benefits of nootropics.

1. Boost Cognitive Performance

One of the most common reasons people use nootropic supplements is to promote brain health. Research shows that nootropics improve mental functions such as memory, attention, motivation, and creativity.

Nootropics may enhance mental performance because they:

  • Improve blood flow to the brain
  • Stimulate the action of neurotransmitters such as glutamate by binding to their receptors
  • Suppress depressant neurotransmitters such as GABA (a chemical in your brain that helps you relax, otherwise known as Gamma-aminobutyric acid).

Apart from boosting mental performance, nootropics may also slow down age-related cognitive decline. Older adults usually experience symptoms of cognitive decline such as memory loss. Nootropic supplements can come in handy in delaying these symptoms.

An excellent, regular source of nootropics is Karmicare’s Awake Morning toothpaste. Awake Morning toothpaste is rich in guarana, a nootropic that will spark your mind to life and keep you active throughout the day.

Infused with lime and mint flavors, Awake Morning toothpaste tastes and smells zesty and fresh, giving you the confident smile you deserve.

2. Improve Sleep Quality

Good sleep is essential for your physical and mental health. Taking a nootropic could help you sleep better.

Research published in the National Library of Medicine supports the use of nootropics like valerian to enhance sleep quality and reduce the symptoms of insomnia. Nootropics promote relaxation and help release anxiety.

This sets the stage for quality sleep. A good night’s sleep comes with other cognitive benefits such as memory formation

Again, with Karmicare’s Asleep evening toothpaste, you can enjoy the best quality sleep just by brushing your teeth before bed. Asleep Evening toothpaste is enriched with valerian, orange essential oil, and cinnamon, three ingredients that help you relax and get in the right state of mind for quality sleep.

3. Increase Attention Span and Concentration

Scientists have proven that nootropics can enhance attention and concentration in kids with attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD). ADHD is a mental condition that makes it difficult to sustain one’s attention on a task.

Aside from their clinical indications, you can use nootropics to enhance your focus and concentration.  According to a 2023 publication in the Journal of Experimental and Basic Medical Sciences, nootropics are instrumental in increasing learning performance and improving attention and concentration. 

In recent times, the internet has popularised the use of nootropics as “study drugs” because they enhance focus, wakefulness, and creativity. Many learners around the world are familiar with the attention-enhancing benefits of drugs like Adderall and modafinil. 

These drugs modify the levels of neurotransmitters such as dopamine and GABA. By doing so, they improve your brain’s alertness and focus.

However, it is important to note that you are more likely to experience side effects while using these drugs. Hence, natural nootropics are advised.

Natural nootropics are the safer alternative because they are free from toxic synthetic compounds and lack side effects associated with high dosages.

4. Ease Stress and Boost Mood

Nootropics can boost your mood and reduce the symptoms of mental anxiety and stress. This is mainly because nootropics increase the level of dopamine, the mood-enhancing chemical in the brain.

Dopamine is the brain’s “reward chemical” and is closely linked to feelings of contentment and pleasure. With little dopamine, you are likely to experience mood swings, lack of focus, or lack of motivation.

Nootropics Help Improve Mental Fatigue

5. Reduce Mental Fatigue

Your brain is a busy factory that uses a lot of energy. It’s common to feel mentally drained to the point where you can barely focus. Mental fatigue affects decision-making, short-term memory, and productivity.

Taking nootropics help keep you moving. 

  • Nootropics improve blood flow to your brain.
  • Facilitate energy production by your brain cells. 
  • Reduce stress hormones that cause fatigue.
  • By relieving brain fatigue, they supercharge your performance and improve your overall quality of life.

Where to Find Nootropics in Everyday Products

If you’re ready to boost your brain power, mood, sleep quality, and focus, here are a few rich sources of nootropics.

1. Guarana

Guarana, also known as Paullinia cupana, is a Brazilian plant found mostly within the Amazon basin. It produces fruits that are harvested for their seeds. One guarana fruit is the size of about 4 coffee beans. Guarana fruits contain black seeds that are usually processed into a powder form called guarana extract.

Guarana is famous for its health benefits. For millennia, Amazonian tribes have used guarana powder to promote good health. Today, guarana extract is a common ingredient in many energy and soft drinks.

Guarana extract is rich in stimulants such as caffeine, theophylline, and theobromine.

The health benefits of guarana are:

  • Improves brain power: Guarana consumption has been shown to boost learning and memory. A study comparing guarana to ginseng, another popular nootropic, showed that guarana was superior in enhancing brain function.
  • Lowers the risk of heart disease: Similar to green tea, guarana contains antioxidants like tannins, saponins, and catechins. Antioxidants lower the risk of heart disease by reducing blood pressure and possibly, by helping to control blood sugar.
  • May promote weight loss: Guarana may help you lose weight and avoid obesity. Studies show that compounds in guarana may suppress genes that take part in fat production.
  • May reduce mental fatigue and help you focus: Guarana is an awesome source of caffeine. Caffeine has stimulating effects that can help you focus and stay alert.

Without a doubt, guarana is one of those healthy foods you want to consume to help you improve both your mental performance and physical health.

But since guarana is mainly added to energy drinks and soft drinks, you risk consuming too much processed sugar and other unhealthy additives in your quest to enjoy guarana benefits.

So where can you find a healthy and regular source of guarana in everyday products? 

Toothpaste is an easy and effective means to add guarana to your routine. Karmicare’s Awake Morning toothpaste is rich in guarana to help you boost your energy levels as you gear up for the day.

For a boost of guarana, choose Karmicare’s Awake Morning toothpaste to ensure you don’t miss out on the awesome benefits of this nootropic.

2. Valerian

Valerian is an herb native to Europe and Northern Asia. It’s a common herbal nootropic used to induce sleep, especially in people with insomnia.

Research shows that taking valerian can help you fall asleep faster and stay asleep longer. In addition, unlike other sleep aids, you can consume valerian without having to worry about side effects.

Apart from promoting healthy sleep, valerian helps to reduce stress and anxiety. We've all had those days where being tired, you can’t seem to fall asleep. Your thoughts are racing and you can't seem to recover from the pressure and anxiety of the day.

Valerian-infused Asleep Evening toothpaste from Karmicare will help you drift into slumberland in no time. 

With superior minerals like nano HAp along with active nootropics, Karmicare helps you achieve an optimum mind and mouth.

Unlike fluoride-based oral hygiene products that disturb your wake/sleep cycles, Karmicare actually harmonizes with your body's circadian rhythms.

3. Caffeine

You’ve probably used caffeine before to stay alert and enhance your performance. Caffeine boosts the activities of both the cardiovascular and central nervous systems, energising your body and brain.

Common sources of caffeine include coffee, tea, guarana, soda, and energy drinks. While taking caffeine-containing products, ensure you keep your caffeine content in check. Consuming too much of substances with high caffeine content can result in dependence and other side effects like insomnia, dehydration, and dizziness.

Other nootropics you should take note of are:

  • L-theanine: Found in tea, L-theanine will help you improve your cognitive performance, boost your immunity, lower your blood pressure, and aid in weight loss as noted in the Journal of Medicinal Food.
  • Creatine: Creatine supplements are mainly used by athletes because they enhance athletic performance, but they may also improve brain health, lower blood sugar, and reduce fatigue as cited here.
  • Bacopa monnieri: This is an herb that may also boost brain function, reduce anxiety, and ease inflammation as highlighted in Neurocognitive Effects of Herbal Extracts.
  • Panax ginseng: Panax ginseng is considered an adaptogen. Adaptogens are substances that are believed to make your body more resistant to stressors. Panax ginseng may also enhance mental performance, reduce inflammation, and boost immunity and energy levels
  • Ginkgo biloba: Ginkgo biloba extract may improve cardiovascular health, reduce inflammation, enhance brain health, and lessen anxiety.
  • Rhodiola rosea: Also an adaptogen, rhodiola rosea may help manage stress and anxiety, reduce the symptoms of depression, and improve brain function.

Are Nootropics Safe to Use?

Yes. Nootropics are safe to use in the correct dosage and with guidance from a health care provider.

It’s important to note that prescription and over-the-counter nootropics will almost always have side effects, especially if consumed in large doses. Therefore, always consult your healthcare provider before using these substances.

The potential side effects of nootropics are:

  • High blood pressure
  • Increased heart rate
  • Addiction
  • Insomnia

Natural nootropics are generally safer because their actions in the body are more subtle compared to pharmaceuticals. Ensure you get your nootropic supplements from reputable manufacturers and distributors. 

In the U.S., for example, the FDA regulates dietary supplements differently from other foods and drugs. It’s easier for unhealthy products to reach the market. Look out for products that undergo independent testing to ascertain their safety profile.

Bottomline

Nootropics are substances that improve cognitive function. They can be used to improve memory, focus, concentration, sleep, and mood.

Generally, natural nootropics are safer than drugs because they are less likely to cause side effects. Be sure to only purchase quality products from reputable manufacturers and sellers.

With different formulations for  morning and evening, Karmicare’s toothpaste set contains nootropics tailored to help you maximize your performance during the day and get quality sleep at night

3-reasons-why-you-should-look-for-an-sls.title: 3 Reasons Why you Should look for an SLS Free Toothpaste

image.alt: SLS-Free Toothpaste is a Healthy Option

3-reasons-why-you-should-look-for-an-sls.content:
Self Reflection:

  • Do I pay attention to the ingredients in my personal care products?
  • Could the ingredients in my toothpaste be harming my oral health?
  • What’s an easy way to upgrade my wellness routine?

Key takeaways:

  • Many commercial toothpastes contain unnecessary additives, like sodium lauryl sulfate (SLS).
  • Glycolipids are a natural, eco-friendly ingredient that can replace common foaming agents such as SLS — yet hardly anyone is using it in their toothpaste.
  • Toothpaste containing sodium lauryl sulfate (or SLS) can compromise oral health.

When was the last time you took a closer look at the ingredient list on your toothpaste?

Believe it or not, you may want to keep an eye out for more than just fluoride.

More people are learning about why they may want to choose fluoride-free toothpaste over standard toothpaste brands. However, another common toothpaste ingredient could sabotage your best efforts at oral care — sodium lauryl sulfate (SLS).

Keep reading to learn more about sodium lauryl sulfate, why you may want to choose an SLS-free toothpaste, and why we use glycolipids in our toothpaste for optimum oral health.

What Is Sodium Lauryl Sulfate (SLS)?

If you’ve spent time reading the ingredient lists on your personal care products, there’s a good chance you’ve seen sodium lauryl sulfate (or SLS) somewhere in the formula. We’re talking shampoos, shaving creams, mouthwash, hair dye, and everything in between; SLS is a fairly common ingredient.

Another place you’re likely to find SLS? Check out your household cleaning products. Yep, you read that right.

The same ingredient in your laundry soap, dishwashing liquid, and bathroom cleaners could lurk in your teeth-whitening toothpaste.

So what’s it doing there?

In a nutshell, sodium lauryl sulfate is a surfactant that acts as an emulsifier.

Think of it this way: When a product contains oil and water, the only way to get those ingredients to blend is to add an element that helps them do exactly that. Even though other ingredients do this (more on that soon), SLS often pops up on those ingredient lists.

It’s not just about SLS acting as a thickener, however; it’s also about it being used as a foaming agent.

Many times, it’s sodium lauryl sulfate that’s responsible for the foamy shampoo experience you get when you wash your hair or dishes.

SLS is responsible for the foamy experience in toothpaste.

While it might seem like the amount of bubbles you see correlates to how clean something is getting, that isn’t necessarily the case.

More often than not, lathering agents are used as a psychological trigger that gives you the illusion that something is being cleaned without actually cleaning.

If your goal is to nurture and support your oral health, you might want to think twice about what you’re putting on your toothbrush. Choosing an SLS-free toothpaste is the first step to take.

3 Reasons Why You Should Choose SLS-Free Toothpaste

Staving off gum disease and maintaining healthy teeth (and a bright smile) doesn’t have to come at the cost of turning to harmful toothpaste brands. Aside from avoiding fluoride, an SLS-free toothpaste may make all the difference in your oral health.

Here are three reasons you may want to avoid products with SLS in your dental health routine.

1. SLS is an Unnecessary Additive

Sometimes it isn’t clear which ingredients do the heavy lifting in your toothpaste, and the more additives and extras in a formulation, the more confusing it can be.

Sodium lauryl sulfate is one of several unnecessary additives, including detergents, dyes, parabens, and other chemical preservatives. It’s important to note that the SLS you see on ingredient lists can be synthetic and petroleum-based or more naturally derived (although this still requires chemical synthesis).

But don’t be fooled into thinking SLS is a must in your toothpaste. It isn’t.

Glycolipids are an excellent sulfate-free swap for the foaming action provided by sodium lauryl sulfate. Even more, it’s 100% biodegradable and more environmentally friendly.

Made from fermented sugars, glycolipids are also biocompatible, so there’s no harm in swallowing (unlike other toothpastes made with fluoride).

FYI: SLS isn’t just lurking in big brands like Colgate and Biotene. Even if you do see a toothpaste that is SLS-free, such as Sensodyne Pronamel, it may not be fluoride-free. SLS can also be in more natural toothpaste such as Tom’s of Maine, so it’s important that you take a few minutes to thoroughly read through the ingredient list before you buy.

2. Support Your Oral Microbiome

Why not skip the chemical cocktail and choose an SLS-free toothpaste? Better yet, pick one with higher quality and more natural ingredients in the first place.

If you visit a natural dentist, they’re likely to recommend looking for products with more recognizable and natural ingredients. Here are some things to keep in mind as you shop:

  • Pass on artificial flavors and look for toothpaste made with pure ingredients. Fresh mint flavoring from peppermint or spearmint is a great option. Xylitol, aloe, baking soda, tea tree, and coconut oil or coconut water are natural ingredients that are more supportive of your oral microbiome than those you may find in standard toothpaste.
  • Regardless of your oral care goals: sensitivity relief, extra whitening, or maintaining fresh breath and healthy gums, a higher concentration of active ingredients will win out over additives and filler ingredients.

You don’t have to stick with SLS-based toothpaste for effective cleaning of your mouth. SLS-free alternatives such as glycolipids are effective and safer.

Karmicare’s Biorhythmic Oral Hygiene Set is the most effective SLS-free toothpaste option for whole body health that extends beyond your mouth.

Shop Karmicare SLS-Free Toothpaste Now

Being natural compounds, glycolipids help maintain a healthy balance in your mouth while being gentle on sensitive tissues. Unlike SLS which can sometimes cause dryness and irritation, glycolipids create a mild, smooth foam that effectively cleans your mouth without irritating.

Pro Tip: Karmicare is safe for the whole family. It’s designed to be left on your teeth instead of going down the drain (like conventional toothpaste with SLS and fluoride). Since it’s safe to swallow, there’s no need to buy a specialty kids' toothpaste, making Karmicare a superior choice in oral care.

Brushing with SLS-free Toothpaste Helps Improve Your Oral Health

3. SLS May Cause Oral Irritation

Despite your resolve to take terrific care of your teeth, the wrong toothpaste formula can undermine your efforts every time you reach for your toothbrush.

SLS is a known irritant and may be causing oral issues you didn't know could be connected to sodium lauryl sulfate.

Using toothpaste with SLS leads to canker sores, dry mouth, bad breath, and sensitive teeth. Sodium lauryl sulfate dries out the tissues of your mouth. When those conditions change, so will the pH of your oral environment, which can lead to those uncomfortable (and downright unpleasant) experiences.

Using toothpaste with SLS can also cause tissue sloughing, which is precisely what it sounds like.

The skin inside your mouth is thin and delicate, hence, the skin of your inner cheeks and lips become more prone to peeling. This results in further discomfort.

Consider switching from your old brand to an SLS-free toothpaste and say goodbye to persistent canker sores and bad breath.

Make That Switch Now

Did You Know?

Karmicare's dental floss contains activated charcoal, so you can safely get an even brighter smile. The charcoal will help lift tea and coffee stains, whiten areas your toothbrush may miss, and eliminate plaque buildup.

Not all toothpastes are created equal. While some toothpastes may appear to support your oral health goals, sometimes they do more harm than good. Being mindful and particular about the ingredients you're using in your toothpaste pays dividends.

Moreso, they can take wellness one step further than oral health and can support your whole body.

morning-and-night-time-brushing-why-timi.title: Morning and Night Time Brushing: Why Timing Matters.

image.alt: Brushing Your Teeth Both Morning and Night Is Important For Your Oral Health.

morning-and-night-time-brushing-why-timi.content:
Oral hygiene is more than just a daily ritual. It is a vital aspect of your overall health and well-being. The mouth is a window to your body, and poor dental care can affect your entire bodily system. Therefore, maintaining a consistent and effective oral care routine - brushing and flossing morning and night - is crucial.

Does the timing of brushing matter?

This guide will explore why brushing in the morning and at night is crucial, and how timing impacts your health, for a clean mouth, fresh breath, and a healthier smile.

Why Brushing in the Morning is Important

Brushing your teeth in the morning is often the first thing people do. No one wants to start the day with an unpleasant morning breath. But morning brushing does more than just freshen your breath; it plays a pivotal role in maintaining oral health.

  • Freshens Breath After a Night's Sleep

Saliva acts as a natural cleanser for your mouth. But during sleep, saliva production reduces. This decrease allows bacteria to multiply, causing 'morning breath'. Brushing your teeth first thing in the morning removes this build-up and ensures a fresh start to your day.

  • Removes Plaque and Bacteria That Build-up Overnight

Bacteria forms a sticky, colourless film called plaque overnight. If left unchecked, plaque can harden into tartar, leading to cavities and gum disease. Morning brushing effectively removes plaque build-up, preventing potential problems.

  • Protects Teeth All Day Long

Beyond simply cleaning your mouth, brushing in the morning protects your teeth throughout the day. Toothpaste containing nano-hydroxyapatite strengthens enamel and prevents cavities. Additionally, it creates a clean surface that makes it harder for bacteria and food particles to stick during the day.

The timing of your morning brushing can greatly affect its effectiveness. A common debate revolves around whether to brush your teeth before or after breakfast. Let's explore the pros and cons of each option.

1. Brushing Before Breakfast

Brushing your teeth before breakfast removes overnight bacteria and plaque, which gives you a clean start. This protects your enamel from sugars and acids in your food. However, some people dislike the lingering taste of toothpaste, which can alter the flavor of their food.

2. Brushing After Breakfast

Brushing after breakfast removes food particles and sugars. This can be especially important if your breakfast includes acidic or sugary foods, which can weaken your enamel. However, brushing immediately after eating acidic foods can harm your enamel. Dentists recommend waiting at least 30 minutes to allow saliva to neutralize the acids and protect your enamel.

Why is Nighttime Brushing Important?

It is important to start your day with a healthy, clean mouth.

While morning brushing is essential for starting your day with a clean mouth, night brushing is equally important.

  • Removes Food Particles and Plaque

Throughout the day, your teeth are exposed to various foods, drinks, and environmental factors that can lead to the buildup of plaque and food particles. Brushing at night removes these elements and prevents them from causing damage to your teeth and gums while you sleep.

  • Reduces Tooth Decay and Gum Disease

Skipping nighttime brushing allows bacteria to linger in your mouth. They produce acids that weaken enamel and irritate your gums. Over time, this can cause cavities, gingivitis, and even more severe forms of gum disease. Brushing before bed removes these harmful substances and reduces the risk of dental problems.

  • Prevents Morning Breath

Bad breath is often caused by bacteria that accumulate in your mouth overnight. Night-time brushing ensures you wake up with fresh breath by reducing the bacteria that cause morning breath.

During the day, the Awake Toothpaste strengthens enamel and fights plaque, while at night, the Asleep Toothpaste remineralizes and soothes your gums. This ensures 24/7 protection. 

Brushing your teeth in the morning and at night is essential for keeping your teeth and gums healthy. Brushing in the morning removes overnight bacteria while brushing at night clears the build-up of the day.

What is Fluoride in Toothpaste?

Fluoride is a natural mineral found in soil and water. It’s a chemical form of fluorine, the thirteenth most abundant element in the periodic table.

Many toothpaste brands have included fluoride in their products for several reasons:

  • Fluoride, especially in combination with other ingredients like zinc citrate, slows down the demineralization of teeth.
  • Fluoride also has antiplaque properties. It prevents tartar from forming when plaque hardens.
  • Some toothpaste combines fluoride with calcium carbonate to effectively remove plaque.
  • Experts also argue that fluoride supports remineralization, the process by which teeth naturally repair themselves.

While fluoride can be useful in toothpaste, it is linked to potential side effects.

This has led many healthcare providers to recommend fluoride-free toothpaste options.

Fluoride Affects Your Oral Health Negatively

Harmful Effects of Fluoride in Toothpaste

Despite the role of fluoride in dental care, it comes with significant downsides.

Did you know? When you brush for 2 minutes, twice a day, as you should, you are exposed to chemicals for 24.3 hours a year. Even when rinsing, your system still absorbs it through the mucous membrane.

1. Fluoride Impairs Sleep Quality

Up to 30% of adults suffer from short-term insomnia.

While stress and screen time can impact your sleep, fluoride might be another culprit.

It disrupts your circadian rhythm, the body’s biological clock that governs your sleep-wake cycle. Fluoride may also calcify the pineal gland and reduce the production of melatonin, the sleep hormone.

2. Fluoride May Cause Dental Fluorosis

Dental fluorosis is the discoloration of the teeth caused by overexposure to fluoride.

Reduced mineralization of teeth causes fluorosis discoloration.

Kids and teenagers are more susceptible to this condition as their teeth are still developing.

Excess fluoride calcifies developing teeth, resulting in discoloration.

While mostly cosmetic, the effects of fluorosis can be damaging to dental health. It can also increase the risk of fractures and secondary complications.

3. Fluoride May Weaken Bones

While fluoride increases bone density, it may also weaken bone quality.

Research shows that bone quality reduces with increasing fluoride content.

Too much fluoride may also lead to skeletal fluorosis. This further weakens the bones.

4. Fluoride May Lead to Reduced IQ in Kids

Studies show that exposure to fluoride during childhood is associated with reduced IQ scores.

Pregnant women who consume fluoride may also extend this risk to their unborn children.

Since children’s brains are still developing, they are at a greater risk of experiencing fluoride neurotoxicity.

5. Fluoride May Disrupt Thyroid Function

The thyroid gland is a small organ located in front of the neck. It produces thyroid hormones, which regulate your body’s metabolic rate.

Fluoride disrupts the production of thyroid hormones. This may lead to hypothyroidism, which affects how the cells in the body process energy.

In 2012, British scientists reported higher levels of hypothyroidism in areas with fluoridated water.

For instance, The American Heart Association reports that gum disease is a significant risk factor for cardiovascular diseases.

Bacteria from gum infections can penetrate the bloodstream and induce inflammation of the blood vessels. This results in arterial plaque - a buildup of substances like fats, cholesterol, and calcium in and on the artery walls.
